title: Review Qualifying Income and Other Criteria for Workfare Income Supplement Scheme
what_it_is: Review Qualifying Income and Other Criteria for Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

sections.label: WIS payouts and income ceiling
sections.summary: In 2017, 407,000 workers received $650 million in WIS payouts, and the qualifying income ceiling was raised three times, most recently on 1 January 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In 2017, 407,000 workers received WIS payouts amounting to $650 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Since inception, the qualifying income ceiling has been raised three times, with the most recent revision being effected on 1 January 2017.

sections.label: Transfers for low-wage older worker
sections.summary: A 65-year-old worker earning $1,200 a month would receive Workfare, Silver Support and GST Vouchers transfers of nearly six months' salary, or $7,000 annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Overall, a 65-year-old worker earning $1,200 a month would receive Government transfers comprising Workfare, Silver Support and GST Vouchers amounting to nearly six months' salary, or $7,000 annually.

sections.label: 20th percentile income growth
sections.summary: Between 2012 and 2017, incomes before Government transfers at the 20th percentile grew 4.2% per annum in real terms, faster than median income growth of 3.4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Between 2012 and 2017, incomes before Government transfers at the 20th percentile of workers grew at 4.2% per annum, or roughly about 20%, over the last five years, faster than median income growth of 3.4%, or about 16%, over the last five years, in real terms.

sections.label: Moving informal workers to formal employment
sections.summary: Informal workers lack formal contracts and are outside CPF, making salaries hard to gauge, so the direction is to move them towards formal employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: If you look at the informal worker today, the challenge is that because they do not have a formal contract and they are outside of the CPF system, it is very difficult to gauge what their monthly salaries are, for example, or if they are contributing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Our long-term goal is really to help them build up their retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Therefore, I think it is better that we move them into formal employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: It is something that we could look at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: But you also have social support, you have formal employment search services that we could provide through WSG and e2i.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Certainly, for such workers, we know they are vulnerable and, therefore, I think the direction is still to move them towards formal employment.
